messages:
IncidentBot: paging: suspicious log export detected from staging -> external IPs, potential auth header leakage. severity=P2. linked alert: https://alerts.redwood.internal/alert/23456
Alice (sre): seeing a spike in 401/403 followed by a handful of 200s with long bearer tokens in logs. looks like masked tokens got dumped in a debug log and rotated into a bundle that left staging buckets.
Bryan (oncall): copied samples to secure channel. @Maria can you confirm whether these tokens were valid for prod service accounts?
Maria (sec-eng): short answer: yes. one of the leaked tokens belonged to a staging service-account that also had cross-environment IAM bindings—incorrectly provisioned last week. we're treating this as credential exposure.
Jasmine (oncall): I'm taking primary on-call. Alice handing off.
Alice (sre): handing off to @Jasmine — I've started an immediate revocation plan for the svc-account and flagged related keys. ps: please pause all non-essential deploys to staging and delay promo to prod.
Jasmine (oncall): acknowledged. @DeployBot, pause staging deploys and freeze promo pipeline.
DeployBot: staging pipeline paused by request of @Jasmine (oncall).
Maria (sec-eng): rotation plan: 1) revoke exposed service-account keys 2) create fresh keys with restricted roles 3) update KeyVault and push secrets to prod-only bindings 4) rotate any tokens seen in customer-facing proxies 5) audit access history and S3 egress logs. I'll run step 1 now.
Maria (sec-eng): revocation command run: ```gcloud iam service-accounts keys disable 0123abcd --project=redwood-staging```
Maria (sec-eng): confirmed disabled key id 0123abcd. risk window minimized but we need to assume leaked artifacts were copied externally earlier today.
Alice (sre): traffic mitigation — added temporary WAF rule to block specific outbound hosts we saw in egress records. also tightened S3 bucket ACLs for the staging artifacts-bucket.
Bryan (oncall): backups: snapshot of staging bucket taken at 1759876700 for forensic analysis. copied to internal-sec-only bucket.
SupportBot: Alert: two customers reported odd auth failures in last hour (ticket #5489, #5490). both on sessions created around 2023-11-02T15:12:xxZ.
Joe (product): are customers impacted? need a short blurb for CS if there is an outage.
Jasmine (oncall): initial customer impact: some legacy tokens (issued to service integrations) may have been revoked as part of rapid mitigation. user-facing flows largely unaffected; background jobs using those tokens may have failed. telling CS to queue a message: "We rotated some integration tokens as a precaution; if you see failures, please reopen a ticket."
Maria (sec-eng): I recommend rotating the prod-facing proxy auth key as well to be safe. creating a dedicated rollout window to avoid cascading failures.
Jasmine (oncall): plan for prod rotation: can we do canonical rolling key swap with automatic fallback? Alice, Bryan help coordinate.
Alice (sre): yes — run new key deployment to canary proxy pool (10% traffic), validate, then promote. rollback if error rate > 1% or latency > 200ms. I'll set canary and monitors.
Bryan (oncall): I'll prepare the rollback playbook and health checks. commands I'll run if things go south: ```curl -f https://canary-proxy/health || kubectl rollout undo deployment/proxy```.
Maria (sec-eng): generating new key: `openssl rand -base64 32` then upload to KMS and set binding. doing that now.
Maria (sec-eng): new proxy key uploaded to KMS and IAM binding set for proxy-canary pool.
DeployBot: canary deployment started for proxy with new key by @Alice (sre).
Alice (sre): canary metrics so far: 0.2% error, latency +10ms. lets let this run for 10 minutes and then promote.
SupportBot: customer ticket update: informed customers that we rotated some integration tokens; monitoring for reopen.
Joe (product): thanks team. can we draft a short timeline for incident log? CS wants ETA for public note.
Maria (sec-eng): ETA for internal postmortem draft: 24 hours. public customer note ETA: 48-72 hours after root cause confirmed and any PI redaction done.
Jasmine (oncall): continuing monitoring. next steps: finish full key rotation for all implicated service-accounts, complete forensic copy, run access audit, and confirm no signs of credential use outside our infra. I'll page @Maria and @Alice if we see traffic to those external hosts again.
Alice (sre): one more check: ensure alerting rules for debug-log exports are tightened so debug logs containing auth headers are never shipped to external buckets. I'll open a config PR to remove PII from debug sinks.
Maria (sec-eng): opened issue #sec-logs-403 to scrub auth headers at emitter level. tagging infra and devex.
Bryan (oncall): handoff: I'm taking second-shift monitoring 12:00-18:00 UTC. Jasmine will continue as primary until rotation complete.
Jasmine (oncall): acknowledged handoff. leaving notes below for next oncall: rotation status=canary stable, revoked keys=0123abcd, forensic snapshot=snap-1759876700, customer-notified=initial.
Alice (sre): thx @Jasmine. I'll stay nearby for rollback support.
Maria (sec-eng): final note for now: if you see tokens in any public repo or paste sites, escalate to legal and file DMCA takedown with support team.
Joe (product): once we have confirmation of containment, I will prepare a short customer-facing message and coordinate with CS.
IncidentBot: incident status changed to "Mitigated" by @Jasmine (oncall).
